areas.summary:
This area implements the `codewatch graph` and `codewatch dashboard` CLI subcommands, layered on `@titan-design/code-graph`'s store: indexing, checks/diffs, coupling and similarity analysis, embeddings, pruning, and dashboard payload assembly for the web view.

Each subcommand lives in its own `graph-*.ts` or `dashboard-*.ts` file exporting a `run*` function plus a `register*Commands(program)` entry point wired from `graph-cli.ts`; shared store access goes through `openGraphStore`/`resolveIndexDbPath` in `utils/graph-store.ts`, which also guards against pre-0.2 legacy DB files via `legacyGraphDbVersion`/`moveLegacyGraphDbAside`. Dashboard commands compose graph data into `DashboardPayload`s windowed by churn period (`computeWindowPayloads`, deduped via `windowSignature`), and each command has a matching test in `__tests__/`.

areas.summary:
This area renders dependency graph snapshots into self-contained interactive HTML (Cytoscape.js), and diffs two snapshots against each other for CI checks and local review.

Entry points sit in `packages/cli/src/commands/graph-render*.ts` and `graph-dashboard.ts`, which call `renderHtml`/`renderMultiViewHtml` from `packages/render/src/template.ts` with a `RenderInput`/`GraphView` built from a graph snapshot. Layout (`layout.ts`), edge routing/weighting (`edge-routing.ts`, `edge-weight.ts`), and collapsing nodes into directories/packages (`collapse-directories.ts`, `collapse-packages.ts`, `focus-package.ts`) are separate pure transforms composed before templating; diffing two snapshots goes through `diff-snapshot.ts` producing `NodeStatus`/`EdgeStatus`/`RenderDiffMeta` that the template overlays (`template-violations.ts`, `CheckDiffOverlay`). New render features should add a pure transform module plus a matching test in `__tests__/`, then wire it into `RenderOptions`/`RenderInput` rather than mutating the Cytoscape template scripts directly.

areas.summary: This area builds and evaluates the graph-context pipeline: a read API over the code graph (`read-api/`), CLI commands that build, format, and bundle context or expose it via MCP (`commands/graph-context-*`, `commands/graph-mcp.ts`, `mcp/server.ts`, `mcp/http-server.ts`), and an offline eval harness (`eval/`) that mines coding tasks, generates an oracle suite with ground truth, retrieves and grades answers against strata like `structurally-hidden`. Add new task types via `TaskType`/`ALL_TASK_TYPES` and new ground-truth shapes via the `GroundTruth` union in `eval/types.ts`, keeping oracle, retrieval, and grader logic in matching `eval/*.ts` + `eval/__tests__/*.test.ts` pairs; new read-only graph queries go through `createReadApi`/`GraphReadApi` in `read-api/`, not ad hoc graph access in commands.

areas.summary: This area implements the `graph arch`, `graph report`, and `graph wiki` CLI commands, which render architecture diagrams, quality/risk reports, and wiki documentation from the code graph store. Each command is split into a `-compute`/context-builder module, one or more `-sections`/`-format` modules for rendering (Mermaid, Markdown, JSON), and a thin `graph-*.ts` entry point that registers the Commander subcommand; shared analysis helpers (hotspot scoring, bus-factor, churn windowing) live in `buildReportContext` and `utils/churn-window.ts` and are looked up via `lookupMetric`/`keepNode` rather than recomputed per section. New report sections or arch views should follow this split-by-concern file layout (compute vs. format vs. sections) to stay under the 350-line `max-file-loc` gate, and every command/section pairs with a test in `__tests__/` (including a `json-parity.test.ts`-style check when adding a new JSON output shape).

areas.summary: This is a static-site React dashboard that renders a single build-time JSON payload (`window.__CODEWATCH__`, typed by `types.ts`) into per-metric views: overview, hotspots, coupling, blast radius, ownership, drift, fitness, and architecture. `App.tsx` owns tab routing and reads `data.ts`/`sample-data.ts` for payload access and dev fixtures; each `views/*.tsx` file is a self-contained tab built from shared pieces in `components/` (primitives, drift badges, dossier metrics, the treemap) and `theme.ts` tokens. To add a new metric view, extend `types.ts` for the new payload shape, add a `views/XView.tsx` following the existing view's layout/data-access pattern, wire it into `App.tsx`'s tab list, and reuse `components/primitives.tsx` rather than introducing new styling primitives.

areas.summary: This fixture corpus provides realistic TypeScript source files (routing, auth, webhook handling, logging middleware) that integration tests run the analyzer against to validate detectors and metrics on non-trivial code. Files follow a `<kind>-<name>.ts` naming convention and export a small set of typed functions per concern; add new fixtures the same way, one concern per file, rather than growing an existing file, and pair any new detector-triggering pattern with a corresponding case here instead of synthetic snippets inline in test code.
